title: Rabbi Yochanan bar Shaul
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman places him, apparently, among the last tannaim, in the generation after Rabbi. In Eruvin 81a, Rabbi Yochanan ben Shaul says, “If its challah portion has been removed,” etc. Dikdukei Soferim and the Rosh read, “Rabbi Yonatan ben Shaul said in the name of Rabbi.” Yuchasin had this reading, citing under Yose ben Shaul and his brother that they were disciples of “דב”; Hyman says this should read “Rabbi.” In Shabbat 125b: “Rabbi Yose ben Shaul says—and Rabbi Yochanan ben Shaul says: a ship’s sounding rod,” etc. Dikdukei Soferim reads Rabbi Yonatan ben Shaul. If he is Rabbi Yonatan ben Shaul, he is mentioned in Sanhedrin 57a: “Rabbi Yonatan ben Shaul says: one who pursues his fellow,” etc. A precious statement of his remains in Sotah 46a: “Why did the Torah say to bring a heifer to a valley? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Let something that has not produced fruit come—and atone for someone whom they did not allow to produce fruit.” In Bereshit Rabbah 94:3 and Midrash Tehillim 105:7, Rabbi Levi speaks in his name.

notes.text: The named Eruvin81a text spells out Yochanan ben Shaul. Hyman’s Yonatan variant and conditional identification are retained separately. The supplied “דב” is the word Hyman proposes correcting to Rabbi, not a person named Dov.
The dash in Hyman’s Sotah quotation omits intervening wording; the English does not silently insert the fuller Talmud passage.

Eruvin 81a directly reads Yochanan ben Shaul in the challah teaching. The adjacent Yose ben Shaul teaching is a separate occurrence. Hyman’s Yonatan variants, conditional identity and proposed correction of דב to Rabbi remain his; the exact Dikdukei Soferim, Rosh and Yuchasin editions were not inspected. The omitted words in the Sotah quotation are not silently supplied.
